Buying guide

Planning your custom gift box project

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

A useful packaging brief connects the product, its journey and the opening experience. Make those decisions first, then compare structures, materials and decoration.

In this guideBuild the brief around the actual productChoose the opening action and delivery formatTurn the idea into a comparable specificationApprove fit before approving decorationDiscuss your packaging →

Build the brief around the actual product

Measure the finished product at its widest points, including caps, handles and accessories. Record its weight and the quantity of pieces in each set. A bottle and a jar may look balanced in a photograph but need different support heights inside the same box. Send a simple arrangement sketch and identify which surfaces should be visible when the lid opens.

Distinguish product dimensions from usable box dimensions. The insert, tissue and clearance all occupy space. Give the packaging designer the product measurements rather than adding an arbitrary allowance to every side. If the product is fragile, include a physical sample so the cradle can be checked around the real shape.

Choose the opening action and delivery format

A magnetic rigid box suits a hinged presentation; a lid-and-base box gives a separate lift-off opening; a drawer reveals the contents along one axis. These choices change the insert access, storage volume and packing sequence. Choose the gesture that suits your product rather than decorating a structure before checking whether it works.

Also decide whether the presentation will travel inside another carton. A retail white-card carton, a gift box and a parcel shipper serve different roles. A coordinated pack may use a folding carton for each item, a rigid gift box for the set and a corrugated case for transport.

Turn the idea into a comparable specification

  • Structure, opening direction and confirmed internal dimensions.
  • Board or paper grade, wrapping paper and surface treatment.
  • Insert layout, material and product orientation.
  • Exterior and interior artwork, print colors and decorative processes.
  • Quantity per size and design, assembly, packing and delivery destination.

Ask the supplier to separate assumptions from confirmed choices. Two quotations are only comparable when they cover the same box, insert, print scope and delivery responsibilities.

Approve fit before approving decoration

Begin with a structural sample when dimensions or closure are uncertain. Place every item into the insert, lift it out and repeat the intended packing sequence. Check access for fingers and whether tissue or an information card interferes with closure.

Then review the decorated sample under consistent light. Record material references, color approvals and any remaining changes in writing. Keep an approved sample and versioned artwork together so production has a single reference. Start with the product catalog or prepare a project brief containing these details.
